summary: You presented a well-motivated Australian reef-monitoring CubeSat mission with a sound sun-synchronous orbit choice, STK access analysis and drag-sail EOL plan. The introduction is strong, but internal contradictions (altitude vs resolution, thrusters at EOL), an incorrect RAAN justification, missing STK scenario files and sub-professional referencing (Wikipedia, bare URLs) held the report back.
next_steps: Fix internal contradictions: clarify that low resolution is undesirable for reef imaging, and rewrite the EOL section so the thruster/descent discussion and drag-sail sentence are consistent and complete.
Replace Wikipedia with primary sources and format all references consistently (authors, titles, dates); number and caption all figures and tables.
Attach your STK scenario files and access reports in an appendix, and add a quantitative recap (orbit elements, access statistics) to strengthen the conclusion.

criteria.C1: Accomplished (8/10). You addressed all required elements: the fluid-lensing reef-monitoring mission, rationale with bleaching statistics, the single-satellite justification, and users/funding (CSIRO, BOM). To reach the top band, sharpen the operator-vs-customer roles and expand the user discussion with more detail and literature support.
criteria.C2: Accomplished (7/10, 42/60). Launch (Vega E from Guiana), orbit (COE table, J2 inclination plot), manoeuvres, ground station with STK access analysis, and 5-year duration with drag-sail EOL are all evidenced. Next level requires: correcting the RAAN justification (RAAN is not set by launch-site longitude; Kourou is ~52°W), resolving the altitude-resolution contradiction, justifying contact-frequency claims quantitatively, and including STK scenario files in an appendix.
criteria.C3: Adequate (7/10). Your conclusions summarise each segment and acknowledge risks such as Vega E availability with a Vega C fallback. To reach Accomplished, add a quantitative recap of key results (orbit elements, access statistics, EOL timeline) and forward recommendations beyond the launch contingency.
criteria.C4: Adequate (5/10). Your structure is logical with headings and an executive summary, but figures and tables lack numbers, references are bare URLs including Wikipedia (explicitly disallowed), and typos/unfinished sentences (e.g. the broken drag-sail sentence) reduce professionalism. Number all figures/tables, fix proofreading, and adopt a consistent citation style to reach the top band.
